findings.title: Card failure lines splice Home Assistant's English exception text into sv/de messages
findings.claim: In the pin_fail and save_fail error states, every sv and de cell (24 of 24: 2 states x 3 viewports x 2 themes x 2 languages) renders a mixed-language failure line such as 'Kunde inte spara: A hot water minimum of 52 °C leaves no deadband ...', because the card prints err.message (the English text Home Assistant formats for a translation_key exception) instead of the integration's own translated exception message.
findings.mechanism: The card's ten failure sites build their line as L('errors.could_not_*', {err: (err && err.message) || err}). For an integration exception raised with translation_domain/translation_key, Home Assistant's websocket error carries `message` formatted from the en translations and the translation fields beside it; the card never reads translation_key and never calls hass.localize, so the localized prefix ('Kunde inte spara:', 'Speichern nicht möglich:') is followed by an English sentence, although translations/sv.json and de.json carry that very exception's message.

evidence.unit: count of sv/de cells whose failure line contains an en exceptions.*.message prefix
evidence.machine: box B10 (4 vCPU, Linux, Chromium 1243 via playwright 1.63.0, Node 22)
evidence.contention_note: ran beside the seat's own full-grid run; a count, contention-immune

findings.instrumented_symbol: custom_components/heatpump_optimizer/www/heatpump-optimizer-card.js:ManualPlan.slotResult (pin) / WhatIfPanel.onSaveSchedule (save) (the `(err && err.message) || err` failure lines, driven through hass.callService rejections)

perturbation.change: --perturb=err_localize: every `(err && err.message) || err` site first reads hass.localize(`component.${err.translation_domain}.exceptions.${err.translation_key}.message`, err.translation_placeholders)

findings.metric_definition: sv/de cells of pin_fail/save_fail whose .wi-pin-result/.wi-result text contains the leading literal of any translations/en.json exceptions.*.message
findings.phenomenon_property: A failure line the card shows in a non-English UI is entirely in that UI's language whenever the integration ships a translation for the error it reports.

null_control.note: a rejection with no translated counterpart (the P9 grid's plain 'Service call failed') leaves 0 lines matching an en exception message: the count is keyed on Home Assistant's translated-exception shape, and en cells are excluded by construction

reproduction_steps: Set the Home Assistant profile language to Svenska
Open the card's dialog, drag a hot-water slot, press the pin button while the integration refuses (e.g. no loaded entry) or save a schedule whose hot-water minimum leaves no deadband
Read the result line: Swedish prefix, English reason
findings.proposed_fix_scope: One helper in the card that turns a service rejection into text: translated exception via hass.localize (after hass.loadBackendTranslation('exceptions', 'heatpump_optimizer')) when translation_key is present, else err.message; used by all ten failure sites.
findings.criteria_statement: D4-criteria 'look professional' (D4.M3 error states; D4-criteria F3 'errors say what to change' in every language)

findings.title: German headline stats at phone width: the two numbers in one row sit 14 px apart
findings.claim: In every state that shows the headline stats (6 states), at 375 px in German, in both themes, the savings and score numbers in one .hl-stats row differ in baseline by 14 px (12 of 12 such rows; 0 of 96 rows in en, sv or at 768/1280 px), because 'Voraussichtliche Einsparung' wraps to two lines and pushes its number down while 'Optimierungswert' stays on one.
findings.mechanism: cardStyleBlock lays .hl-stat out as label (display:block) then .hl-value (display:block; margin-top:2px): each value hangs from its own label's last line, so a row whose labels wrap to different line counts has its numbers at different heights. The grid stretches the cells to one height but nothing aligns the values to a common line.

findings.title: Tooltip, picker-note and layout-verdict text renders below the card's own 12 px type floor
findings.claim: Across the 900-cell grid, 78 cells render text below 12 px, the smallest step of the card's --hpo-text scale and the floor its other small text keeps with max(12px, ...): the chart tooltip at 10.92 px and its shared-step note at 9.28 px in the phone-width dialog, the shared-step note at 10.95 px at 768/1280 px, the entity picker's note (.sp-note) at 11.2 px and the layout verdict at 11.9 px at every viewport.
findings.mechanism: These rules size type as a bare em multiple of an already reduced parent (dialog.expanded .tooltip { font-size: 0.78em } under @media (max-width: 600px), .tooltip .tt-shared { font-size: 0.85em }, .sp-note and .layout-verdict.match at 0.8/0.85 em), without the max(12px, ...) guard the stylesheet applies in 13 other places, so the product falls under the scale's floor.

findings.title: One status role, two colours: error, success and warning each render in two shades across states
findings.claim: Within one theme, the error role renders as #b3261e (status pill tone-crit, status_fallback) and #ca4c46 (pin/save failure lines and dearer deltas), success as #1c7350 (pill) and #24845d (cheaper/saved lines, light), and warning as #8a5a00 (pill tone-warn) and #ffa600 (the wood alert's stripe, the same in dark): 5 (theme, role) pairs with two colours across the 50 states.
findings.mechanism: The token layer (CARD_TOKENS --hpo-crit/--hpo-ok/--hpo-warn) drives the status pill, while the what-if result lines take the older ERROR_READABLE/SUCCESS_READABLE constants interpolated into cardStyleBlock, and the wood/space-blocked alerts carry inline styles reading Home Assistant's --warning-color directly (border-left:3px solid var(--warning-color,#d98e00)), so one meaning is painted from three palettes.

findings.title: Rendered type and spacing mostly bypass the --hpo-text / --hpo-space scales
findings.claim: Across 50 states x 3 viewports x 2 themes x 3 languages the card renders 17 distinct font sizes outside its 4-step type scale {12, 13, 15, 18 px} (9.28 to 19.6 px; e.g. every what-if button at 14 px, legend chips at 16 px, dialog tabs at 16.66 px, the title at 19.6 px) and 45 distinct non-zero padding/margin/gap values outside its 5-step space scale {4, 8, 12, 16, 24 px}.
findings.mechanism: The token layer (CARD_SCALE_TOKENS) is read by a minority of rules: of 83 font-size declarations most are em multipliers (0.78em, 0.82em, 0.85em, 0.9em, 1.1em, 1.25em, 1.4em ...) and literal px, and paddings/gaps are em or literal px (3px 10px, 6px 8px, 0.45em 0.7em ...), so the computed sizes scatter between and beyond the steps.

findings.title: Six first-run setup page titles are Title Case among sentence-case titles (en; three in sv)
findings.claim: Of the 41 config/options page titles in translations/en.json, 6 -- all on the first-run path (user 'Heat Pump Optimizer Setup', temperature 'Temperature Settings', thermal, zones, dhw, weather_sensitivity) -- are Title Case while the rest read in sentence case ('Your building', 'Heat Pump Optimizer options'); sv carries 3 of the same pattern ('Termisk modell & Optimering', 'Värmepumpsoptimering - Konfiguration', 'Tvåzons- & Solkonfiguration').
findings.mechanism: The older initial-flow step titles were written in Title Case and translated literally; the later pages (building, options) follow sentence case, the Home Assistant UI convention, so a new user meets both styles in consecutive pages.

findings.title: German text mixes „typographic“ and "straight" quotes; a blueprint writes degrees as '15 C'
findings.claim: In German, 27 quoted spans across translations/de.json and the card's STRINGS use straight ASCII quotes while 95 use „…“ (25 of the 27 in de.json, e.g. exceptions.config_entry_not_loaded); and blueprints/automation/economy_mode_on_price_peak.yaml's description writes '1.5 C' and '15 C' where every other surface writes °C.
findings.mechanism: Strings were translated at different times by different passes: some kept the English source's ASCII quotes around placeholders and option names, others used German typography; the blueprint description is plain text written without the degree sign.

Opening the Savings page shows the focus ring on the Plan tab while Savings is the active tab (two tabs outlined, savings_empty screenshot); F2 'visible focus' vs active-state ambiguity, unmeasured here.
